title: new16; unfixed in every release
live_proof: inspection in the 3.22.0 tree: nodeWrite() inserts the node into the hash with no check for iNode==0, while nodeHashDelete() keys off iNode and treats 0 as 'not in the hash', so nodeRelease() frees a block that stays linked in aHash[0]. Fixed upstream in d21bd37c7c; the note recorded with the entry is that it is unfixed in every release up to the one we checked
object: an RtreeNode linked into aHash[0] while still carrying iNode==0
lifetime_ender: nodeRelease() frees the block, but nodeHashDelete() cannot unlink it because it keys off an iNode of 0
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator, with an unusual precondition that is part of the defect rather than an artifact: the %_node INSERT must be suppressed by a BEFORE INSERT trigger raising IGNORE, and no other rowid insert may have happened on the connection, so that last_insert_rowid() returns 0

status: re-measured on all four readings 2026-10-16 on this platform, and two verdicts change. host ASan is the 2026-10-11 bundle's reading and still applies, because case.c has not changed since 7517a8c2fd5e (2026-10-11) and the amalgamation is the same sha256 7fc92e19: heap-use-after-free, READ of size 8 eight bytes into a 1000-byte region (RtreeNode.iNode), nodeHashLookup <- nodeAcquire <- rtreeFilter, freed by nodeRelease <- SplitNode <- rtreeInsertCell, allocated by nodeNew <- SplitNode <- rtreeInsertCell. It could not be re-run: this host currently has no x86 ASan runtime. virtual-malloc NO-READING:unattributed, cause=24 pc=0x3f9ae17800 offset 144 in nodeRelease at fault ADDRESS 0x17, both controls as declared; virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT, cause=25 pc=0x3fafa1b378 offset 240 in nodeHashLookup at fault address 0x3fafb1fe20, both controls as declared; cheribsd-revocation faults SIGPROT(34) si_code=2 PROT_CHERI_TAG/untagged-deref pc=0x1d09a4 = nodeRelease+0x2e, exit 162, with the boot's positive control trapping and revocation knobs 1/0. Every precondition is met in every run: inserted=39, rows=39, nodes before=1, trigger rc=0, db2 nodes=1, split insert rc=0 and db2 nodes after=1, so the BEFORE INSERT trigger really did swallow the %_node write and iNode stayed 0. Only the Sublet reading is a detection; see note. The earlier status text said cheribsd-revocation had no verdict, which was a stale 2026-10-04/05 line: the 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-06 runs both record FAULT SIGPROT(34). The arms block is the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends
note: Re-measured 2026-10-16. The defect is real and worse than a stale read, and the base and CheriBSD cells are NOT detections. (1) The defect, measured as a boolean by new probe site 55: HASHINS p=0x20d400 iNode=0 bucket=0, then DELSKIP p=0x20d400 iNode=0 NOT unlinked, then FREE p=0x20d400 iNode=0 still_in_bucket=1 -- the block goes back to the pool while it is still the head of aHash[0]. In the dangling-hash query the bucket walk then matches it (LOOKUP want=0 bucket=0 head=0x20d400 head_iNode=0, since the dead node's iNode is 0 and that is what is being looked up) and nodeAcquire hands it back out as a live node: HANDOUT p=0x20d400 iNode=0 nRef_read=0 <- returned as live, which also WRITES nRef++ into the dead block. So the program operates on a freed object as if it were alive, and the record's 'reads p->iNode out of freed memory' understates it. (2) Neither non-Sublet arm can see any of that. Under the 16-byte-pointer layout iNode is at offset 16 and nRef at offset 24, and memsys5's Mem5Link is 8 bytes at offset 0, so neither field is touched by the free and neither access has anything to trap on: probe site 55 witnesses both (kind=UAF n=8 and kind=UAF n=4) with tag=1 and cb=0x1e5c00+262144, a capability bounded to the whole 256 KiB sqlite_heap[]. (3) What both arms do fault on is case 15's artifact, reached by a longer route. The dead node, now held with nRef=1, is eventually released: nodeRelease does nRef-- to 0, iNode is 0 so the iNode==1 branch is skipped, and then if( pNode->pParent ) reads offset 0 -- the one field Mem5Link overwrote, tag cleared -- and recurses into it. Base Capstone's fault address is 0x17, which is (-1) + 24, the same value and the same instruction as case 15; CheriBSD's pc resolves to nodeRelease+0x2e, also the same instruction. Site 55 does not print pParent, but 0x17 admits no other reading, and site 54 printed the 0xffffffffffffffff directly in case 15. (4) nodeAcquire would have repaired the field and removed even that fault, had the terminator been 0: its hash-hit path is if( pParent && !pNode->pParent ){ ... pNode->pParent = pParent; }, and -1 is non-zero, so the assignment is skipped and the -1 survives into the release. With a 0 terminator both arms would have completed silently. (5) nodeRelease is not in this case's fault_sites, so the judge already calls the base arm NO-READING:unattributed, and did so in the 2026-10-11 bundle; the cheribsd-revocation cell was never held to the same rule and results/matrix.tsv records it as detected. Both physical rows are marked there, and the physical sublet row is marked too: it is one of the 28 halts at kernel pc 0x800239e4, so this review relies on the virtual arm's cause 25 at nodeHashLookup. Second instance of the Mem5Link false positive after case 15; the family is listed in that case's PROVENANCE.md and in the cross-case note here
fault_sites_why: The next nodeAcquire walks the aHash bucket that still holds the freed node and reads p->iNode out of freed memory (PROVENANCE.md); the bucket walk is nodeHashLookup. Declared 2026-10-10 after the virtual runs resolved faults there; the reason is the source and PROVENANCE.md cited, which predate those runs. CONFIRMED 2026-10-16 by probe site 55, which witnesses both accesses in the dangling-hash query -- the 8-byte iNode read in the bucket walk and the 4-byte nRef read-modify-write in nodeAcquire -- on the same block the FREE hook recorded. The declaration is also what makes the base arm's NO-READING correct rather than lucky: the base and CheriBSD faults land in nodeRelease, which is deliberately not listed here, because the stale accesses this case is about are the two above.
